# `sandloom.sdk.module`

Modules: `define_module`, the L2 `register` form (`ModuleAPI`,
`ModuleDescriptor`), requirements, health and loader results.

Public API 1.0 (spec §2.2, Appendix C).

`from sandloom.sdk.module import <name>`. Signatures in a terminal: `sandloom docs <name>`. Beginner names are the ones generated code and the examples use; any other name is advanced (mark its import line `# sandloom: advanced <reason>` in generated code and examples).

## Beginner names

### `define_module`

```python
def define_module(
    package: str | None = None,
    /,
    *,
    version: str = '0.1.0',
    optional: bool = False,
    consumes: Sequence[Any] = (),
    capabilities: Sequence[Any] = (),
    depends_on: Sequence[str] = (),
    migrations_database: str | None = None,
    migrations_chain: str | None = None,
    health_check: Any | None = None,
    setup: Callable[[ModuleAPI], None] | None = None,
    name: str | None = None,
    router: Any = 'auto',
    events: Any = 'auto',
    issues_tokens: bool = False,
) -> Callable[[ModuleAPI], Any]
```

Build a module's `register(core)` from its declarations (spec §5.7).

In the module's `__init__.py`:

```python
from sandloom.sdk import define_module

register = define_module(__name__, version="0.1.0")
```

Everything the module declares in its conventional submodules is
discovered (routers, events, consumers, contracts, sagas, projections,
consumed contracts). `setup(core)` stays for what has no declaration
(startup tasks, claims contributors, planner operations). `router=` /
`events=` override discovery as today; `consumes` adds to the derived
requirements. Modules are REQUIRED unless `optional=True`.

## Advanced names

### `AUTO`

```python
AUTO: str = 'auto'
```

*(no docstring)*

### `CapabilityRequirement`

```python
class CapabilityRequirement(
    capability: str,
    instance: str = 'default',
    version: str = 'v1',
    features: frozenset[str] = <factory>,
    required: bool = True,
) -> None
```

An infrastructure capability a module needs to function.

Declared on the `ModuleDescriptor` so the loader can preflight — at
startup, before serving traffic — that the capability exists, has a
configured instance backed by a registered driver, and that the driver
supports every required feature. A `required` requirement that cannot be
satisfied fails the module load (and aborts startup if the module itself is
required); an optional one only logs a warning.

### `ContractRequirement`

```python
class ContractRequirement(
    name: str,
    required: bool = True,
    reason: str = '',
    methods: tuple[str, ...] = (),
) -> None
```

A sync service contract a module CALLS (`core.get_service(name)`).

Declared on `ModuleDescriptor.consumes` so the loader can check at
startup — not at the first request — that every consumed contract is
either provided by a module loaded in this process or bound remotely in
`SERVICE_BINDINGS`. A `required` contract that is neither aborts
startup (`ContractBindingError`); an optional one (the module degrades
explicitly without it) only logs a warning. Access facts owned elsewhere
are consumed through the owner's `<owner>.facts.v1` contract:
`ContractRequirement("billing.facts.v1")`.

### `ModuleAPI`

```python
class ModuleAPI(
    facade: CoreFacade,
    *,
    draft: ModuleRegistrationDraft | None = None,
) -> None
```

Stable, minimal registration surface for business modules.

When constructed with a `draft` (the loader's transactional path) write
methods buffer into it and are applied only on a successful commit; read
methods always reflect the live facade. Without a draft (direct use in
tests) writes apply to the facade immediately, preserving the simple API.

`database` overrides the database the contract runtime opens the
provider's Unit of Work on; by default it is the database the module's
descriptor declares (`ModuleDescriptor.database_instances()`).

#### `ModuleAPI.add_claims_contributor`

```python
def add_claims_contributor(self, fn: Any, *, critical: bool = False) -> None
```

Register a contributor of JWT claims (`async (user_id) -> dict`).

The contributor runs in the module's OWN Unit of Work on its own
database (read it with `contract_session`); it is also exposed as
the `<module>.claims.v1` contract so a token issuer in another process
can collect it over RPC (`SERVICE_BINDINGS`). `critical=True`
aborts token minting (503) if the contributor fails (use for security
claims like roles/permissions and tenant allowlists).

#### `ModuleAPI.register_event_consumer`

```python
def register_event_consumer(
    self,
    channel: str,
    handler: Any,
    *,
    name: str,
    durable: bool = True,
    database: str = 'default',
    required: bool = True,
    group: str | None = None,
    start_from: str = 'earliest',
    bind_tenant_from: str | None = None,
    dead_letter: bool = True,
) -> None
```

Subscribe `handler` to `channel` as a durable consumer.

The sanctioned "react to another module's event with a side effect"
path: at startup the framework subscribes the handler under its own
durable consumer group `<module>:<name>` (namespaced by the
registering module, so two modules — or this module deployed in two
services — never share a group and split its events) and runs each
delivery in a Unit of Work on `database` (commit on success,
rollback+redelivery on error). With `durable` (default) the event id
is claimed for exactly-once apply. `required=True` (default) gates
application readiness on the live subscription; mark deliberately
best-effort consumers optional.

`group` pins an explicit group id instead (e.g. the bare pre-0.4
name, to keep draining an existing group). `start_from` applies when
the group is first created: `"earliest"` (default; every event still
within `EVENT_STREAM_RETENTION_SECONDS`), `"latest"` or an ISO-8601
timestamp. `bind_tenant_from` (opt-in) names the payload field holding
the tenant id: the handler then runs with that tenant bound, so
`TenantScoped` code works; a missing/invalid value fails the delivery.
The handler signature is `async (session, envelope) -> None`.
`dead_letter=False` retries a failing delivery FOREVER (capped
backoff) instead of dead-lettering it after the delivery budget — for
effects that must never be silently parked; the handler raises
`PoisonEventError` (`sandloom.core.di`) for an event that can never
apply, which is dead-lettered at once with a CRITICAL log.

#### `ModuleAPI.register_saga`

```python
def register_saga(self, definition: Any) -> None
```

Register a saga this module owns (`sandloom.core.module_api.Saga`).

Binds it to the module (`saga_type = "<module>.<name>"`) and adds a
`ContractRequirement(name, methods=...)` for every contract its
steps call to the module's `consumes` — a missing provider is then a
`ContractBindingError` at startup. The kernel checks the calls
against the providers' describe documents once every module loaded
and installs the advance consumer `<module>:sagas@advance` and the
timer sweep.

#### `ModuleAPI.register_access_fact`

```python
def register_access_fact(self, fact: Any) -> None
```

Register an `sandloom.shared.authz.facts.AccessFact`.

Binds a fact name to its claim/projection/live resolution paths so

#### `ModuleAPI.register_operations`

```python
def register_operations(self, *operations: Any) -> None
```

Declare this module's planner operations (`ReadOperation` /
`JoinRead`): each is planned at startup (a `critical` startup task,
so a declaration that does not match the schema fails the boot), the
chosen executor and the reason are logged, and `/diagnostics/core`
lists them (`planner`).

### `ModuleDescriptor`

```python
class ModuleDescriptor(
    name: str,
    version: str,
    optional: bool = False,
    routes: APIRouter | None = None,
    health_check: HealthCheck | None = None,
    migrations_path: str | None = None,
    depends_on: list[str] = <factory>,
    capabilities: list[CapabilityRequirement] = <factory>,
    migrations_database: str | None = None,
    migrations_chain: str | None = None,
    consumes: list[ContractRequirement] = <factory>,
    issues_tokens: bool = False,
) -> None
```

What a module returns from `register(core)` to describe itself.

Carries the module's identity (`name`/`version`), whether it is
`optional` (modules are required by default: a load failure aborts
startup unless the module says `optional=True`), its `routes`, an
optional `health_check`, its `migrations_path` and `depends_on`
ordering, and the `capabilities` it needs. Reference other modules'
entities by plain UUID — never declare cross-module foreign keys.

#### `ModuleDescriptor.effective_capabilities`

```python
def effective_capabilities(self) -> list[CapabilityRequirement]
```

Capabilities to preflight at load (the declared list).

#### `ModuleDescriptor.migration_chain_key`

```python
def migration_chain_key(self) -> str
```

Key of this module's migration chain (version-table suffix).

#### `ModuleDescriptor.database_instances`

```python
def database_instances(self) -> set[str]
```

The database instance this module's tables live in (one element).

Resolution:

1. `migrations_database` when set (explicit, always wins);
2. otherwise the instances of the REQUIRED `database` requirements:
   none -> `default`; exactly one -> that one; several -> `default`
   if it is among them (a module that reads `default` and also uses
   `analytics` keeps its tables in `default`), else ambiguous ->
   `MigrationTargetError` (declare `migrations_database`).

Optional (`required=False`) database requirements never host the
chain, so an optional, unconfigured instance cannot break
`upgrade-all`. A module's chain is applied to exactly ONE database —
applying it to every declared instance duplicated its tables.
